title: Israel approves plan to establish 13 new settlements in occupied West Bank
facts: Israel’s Security Cabinet approved a plan to establish 13 new settlements in the central occupied West Bank on July 2, 2026.
The new Israeli settlements are planned for the Binyamin regional area in the occupied West Bank.
The Binyamin regional area is situated along Route 60 in the occupied West Bank.
Route 60 is a central north-south artery running through the West Bank that links Palestinian cities such as Nablus, Ramallah, and Bethlehem.
The first phase of the settlement plan includes the establishment of four to six new settlements in the West Bank.
Several existing pastoral outposts in the West Bank are slated for formal legalisation under the newly approved Israeli plan.
The newly approved Israeli settlement plan targets areas northwest of Jerusalem and west of Ramallah.
The newly approved Israeli settlement plan extends eastward towards the Jordan Valley.
The Palestinian Forum for Israeli Studies reported that the number of new settlement outposts reached 86 during 2025.
The number of new Israeli settlement outposts established in the West Bank jumped from 32 in 2023 to 62 in 2024.
Between 2012 and 2022, Israel established an average of approximately eight settlement outposts annually in the West Bank.
The Israeli government allocated 28 million shekels to settlement outposts in 2023.
The Israeli government increased its funding for settlement outposts to 75 million shekels in 2024.
Settlement movements are reportedly preparing to target Area A, a territory under full Palestinian control according to the Oslo Accords.
More than 700,000 Israeli settlers currently live in the West Bank and East Jerusalem territories captured by Israel in 1967.
